question: As per the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, Schedule B comprises of _________ industries.
solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution 1956** was a significant policy document for industrial development in India.
 
• The policy classified industries into three schedules: **Schedule A, Schedule B, and Schedule C**.
 
• **Schedule B** consists of **12 industries** that would be progressively state-owned, but private sector participation would also be allowed.
 
• This schedule includes industries of basic and strategic importance, but the state does not have exclusive rights over them.
 
• The primary goal was to ensure a balanced industrial growth through the involvement of both public and private sectors.
 
• Examples of industries in Schedule B include **fertilizers, road transport, and other industries of national importance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Schedule A**__

 __
 
• **Schedule A** consists of industries that were to be the exclusive responsibility of the state.
 
• It included **17 industries** such as arms and ammunition, atomic energy, railways, and air transport.
 
• The aim was to ensure state control over key sectors of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Schedule C**__
 
 
• **Schedule C** included all other industries not listed in Schedules A and B.
 
• These industries were left open to the private sector with the state facilitating their growth.
 
• The focus was on promoting private investment and entrepreneurship.
